name: Colorful Tree Again
description: An edge-weighted tree of $$$n$$$ nodes is given with each edge colored in some color. Each node of this tree can be blocked or unblocked, all nodes are unblocked initially. A simple path is a path in a graph that does not have repeating nodes. The length of a path is defined as the sum of weights of all edges on the path. A path is good when it is a simple path consisting of edges of the same color $$$c$$$, all edges of color $$$c$$$ are on this path, and every node on the path is unblocked. You need to operate $$$2$$$ kinds of queries: block a node, unblock a node. After each query, print the maximum length among all good paths. If there are no good paths, print $$$0$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \leq n,q \leq 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of nodes and the number of queries. Then $$$n-1$$$ lines follow, each containing four integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$, $$$w$$$ and $$$c$$$ ($$$1 \leq u,v,w,c \leq n$$$; $$$u \not = v$$$), denoting a weighted edge connecting node $$$u$$$ and node $$$v$$$ with weight $$$w$$$ and color $$$c$$$. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree. Then $$$q$$$ lines follow, each containing two integers $$$p$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$p = 0$$$ or $$$p = 1$$$, $$$1\leq x\leq n$$$), denoting a query: if $$$p = 0$$$, block the node $$$x$$$. It's guaranteed that it's not blocked at this time; if $$$p = 1$$$, unblock the node $$$x$$$. It's guaranteed that it's blocked at this time.
output_specification: For each query, print the maximum length of a good path. If there are no good paths, print $$$0$$$.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1787G — Colorful Tree Again [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
